summary: The Philippines admits citizens of more than 150 countries visa-free for 30 days — extendable by 29 days at a Bureau of Immigration office — and requires every arriving traveler to register on the free eTravel platform within 72 hours before arrival. Airlines strictly check onward tickets before boarding.

declarations.text: Every traveler arriving in the Philippines (foreigners and Filipinos alike) must register on the eTravel platform within 72 hours before arrival and present the QR code at check-in and immigration. It is completely free. Use only etravel.gov.ph.

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency over 10,000 USD (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure. Bringing in or taking out more than 50,000 PHP in Philippine currency requires prior authorization from the central bank (BSP).

notes: The UK government says there are strict rules on goods taken into or out of the Philippines, and you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

payments.text: No official source we checked describes card acceptance in the Philippines. Canada's travel advice says ATMs are available in larger cities but may be scarce in rural areas, so have cash in pesos when you travel outside larger urban areas.

safety.text: Most tourist areas of the Philippines are generally safe with normal precautions, though petty theft occurs in cities. Western governments advise against travel to parts of Mindanao and the Sulu archipelago due to terrorism and kidnapping risk.

tips.text: Book an onward or return ticket before you fly: the UK government says most visitors are expected to have proof of return or onward travel and that immigration officials and airlines may ask for it.
Register only on the official eTravel portal, etravel.gov.ph.
Long stays are easy: after the initial 30 days you can keep extending at Bureau of Immigration offices (first a 29-day visa waiver, then 1–6 month extensions), for years in total.

The UK government says around 20 typhoons hit the Philippines each year, mostly between June and November, and Canada says authorities may suspend ferry services at short notice when a storm signal is raised, which can strand you at a port for days. Build slack into island-hopping plans.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for the Philippines?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders enter visa-free for up to 30 days with a passport valid 6 months and an onward ticket. The stay can be extended by 29 days (and beyond) at Bureau of Immigration offices. Everyone must also register on eTravel within 72 hours before arrival.

faq.question: What is eTravel and who needs it?
faq.answer: eTravel (etravel.gov.ph) is the Philippines' free online arrival registration combining immigration, health and customs declarations. Every arriving traveler — foreign or Filipino — must complete it within 72 hours before arrival and show the QR code at check-in and on arrival.

faq.question: Is an onward ticket really required for the Philippines?
faq.answer: Plan on it. The UK government says most visitors are expected to have proof of return or onward travel and that immigration officials and airlines may ask for it, and Canada says customs officials may ask to see a return or onward ticket.

faq.question: How do I extend my stay in the Philippines?
faq.answer: Apply at any Bureau of Immigration office (or the BI e-services portal) before your current stay expires. The first step is a 29-day visa waiver (PHP 3,030); after that you can extend in 1, 2 or 6-month increments, generally up to 36 months total for visa-free nationals.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for the Philippines?
faq.answer: No, not for short visits. Indian passport holders can enter visa-free for 14 days for tourism or business (not extendable), with a passport valid 6 months beyond the stay, a confirmed hotel booking, proof of funds and a return or onward ticket. Those holding a valid US, UK, Schengen, Japanese, Australian, Canadian or Singapore visa or residence permit can instead stay 30 days for tourism, also not extendable. Longer stays need a temporary visitor (9a) visa. Confirm current rules with the Bureau of Immigration before booking.
